pr.title: gh-143005: prevent incompatible __class__ reassignment for ctypes arrays
pr.body:
This PR fixes a heap buffer overflow in ctypes arrays caused by assigning
__class__ to an incompatible array type.

The change rejects __class__ reassignment when the new array type differs
in length, size, or element type, preventing out-of-bounds memory access.
A regression test is included.

<!-- gh-issue-number: gh-143005 -->
* Issue: gh-143005
<!-- /gh-issue-number -->

+    def test_ctypes_array_class_assignment_non_ctypes_target(self):
+        A = c_int * 3

+            a.__class__ = Dummy
+
+    def test_ctypes_array_class_assignment_abstract_target(self):
+        A = c_int * 3
+        a = A()
+        AbstractArray = PyCArrayType.__new__(PyCArrayType, "AbstractArray", (Array,), {})
+
+        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
+            a.__class__ = AbstractArray
+
+    def test_ctypes_array_class_assignment_same_size_ints(self):
+        if sizeof(c_int) != sizeof(c_long):
+            self.skipTest("sizes differ on this platform")
+        A = c_int * 3
+        B = c_long * 3

+        a.__class__ = B

+    def test_ctypes_array_class_assignment_structs(self):
+        class S1(Structure):
+            _fields_ = [("x", c_int)]
+        A = S1 * 2
+        B = S1 * 2
+        a = A()
+        a.__class__ = B
+
+    def test_ctypes_array_class_assignment_pointer_arrays(self):
+        from ctypes import POINTER
+        A = POINTER(c_int) * 2

+        a = A()
+        a.__class__ = B
+
+    def test_ctypes_array_from_param_incompatible(self):
+        A = c_int * 3
+        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
+            A.from_param(object())

+Fix a memory safety issue in ctypes arrays by rejecting ``__class__``
+assignment to incompatible array types.

review_comments.body: You can use `PyUnicode_EqualToUTF8()` or even `_PyUnicode_EqualToASCIIString()` which are more efficient.
What if `new_info` is NULL (abstract class?)? Please add a test for such case.
In what case `length` can be negative? Can we add tests for such cases?
Please avoid using non-ASCII characters in comments, unless this is necessary.

review_comments.body: What happens if the length is 0 (`c_long * 0`)? What happens if one side is `c_long` and other side is `c_ulong`? What happens if one side is `c_double` and other side is `c_int`/`c_long`/`c_longlong`? What happens if one side is not an array?
Why changing `CDataType.from_param` is necessary? Was not changing `PyCArray_setattro` enough?
If `PyStgInfo_FromObject()` returns -1, it sets an error. We should leave the function immediately.
What if only one of them is NULL? Please add tests.

Thank you for the review and confirmation.
I’ll switch to _PyUnicode_EqualToASCIIString() for the __class__ check and add more targeted tests to cover the different failure conditions.

new_info can be NULL for abstract/incomplete array classes where storage info is not initialized yet. I’ll add test to cover this case.
A negative length corresponds to non-array CData types; I’ll also add a test exercising that branch to ensure it is handled safely.

review_comments.body: I think to allow reassignment only when both sides are concrete arrays with identical layout. I will add targeted tests to clarify behavior for zero-length arrays, differing element types (e.g. c_long vs c_ulong, c_double vs integer types), and the case where the target is not an array.

You are right — after re-evaluating the code paths, guarding PyCArray_setattro is sufficient to prevent incompatible __class__ reassignment for array instances.

The change in CDataType.from_param is not strictly required for this fix, so I will drop it and keep the fix localized to PyCArray_setattro.
You are right — if PyStgInfo_FromObject() fails, the error should be propagated immediately. I’ve updated the code to return early on error instead of continuing.

If only one side has storage info, reassignment should be rejected.

I’ll add tests covering both cases: assigning a concrete array instance to an abstract array class, assigning an instance without array storage info to a concrete array class.

review_comments.body:
c_int and c_double most likely have different size. We need to test different types with the same size. I suggest to unite multiple tests in the same method and use a loop with an array of type pairs:
```py
for A, B in [
    (c_int * 3, c_double * 3),
    (c_long * 3, c_double * 3),
    (c_longlong * 3, c_double * 3),
    ...
]:
    with self.subTest(A=A, B=B):
        a = A()
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            a.__class__ = B
```
You can also use `test.support.subTests`.

review_comments.body: Does it work for different structs with the same definition?

issue_comments.body: What if we simply expose `__class__` as a getset? isn't it possible?

There are problems with such special names. If we expose `__class__` as a getset, then `c_long.__class__` will be not a type of `c_long` (the same as `type(c_long)`), but a descriptor. This will confuse much code.
Arf yes you are right. It just feels to me that it is an overkill but I do not think we have a better alternative, do we?

Thanks for the discussion

I agree exposing ``__class__`` as getset would be problematic since it would turn
``type(obj).__class__`` into  descriptor and break expectations.

Given that validating reassignment in ``tp_setattro`` seems like least disruptive
approach. I will follow up with additional tests to cover the remaining edge cases
(abstract targets, non-array targets, zero-length arrays, etc.) if you suggest.
@serhiy-storchaka Do i add more test case as we discuss or how to proceed?

Are there tests for `old_info == NULL`, `new_info == NULL`, `old_info->length < 0`, `new_info->length < 0`? Add tests for successful `__class__` assignments. For example, `c_int`, `c_long` and `c_longlong` should be compatible if they have the same size (and `ssize_t` should be compatible with one of them). Are `c_long` and `c_ulong` compatible? What about arrays of structures? Arrays of pointers of different type?

Since there are changes in `from_param()`, tests for `from_param()` are also needed.
